summary: Chinese stocks post their best day in two years after Beijing promises state buying, and Huawei hints at a memory chip to rival South Korea's.
body: Chinese stocks jumped on Friday after a cabinet meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang said state-backed investors, known as the "national team", would do more to steady markets. Chinese state media says it was the first time the phrase appeared in such a statement.[^2] Central Huijin, a state investment company, will act as a kind of stabilisation fund that buys when markets panic.[^1][^2] The Shanghai Composite rose 3.7% and the tech-heavy STAR 50 index 15%, their best days since October 2024, after falling from July on weak consumer spending, a long property slump and a global sell-off in AI stocks.[^1][^2] Saxo Bank's Charu Chanana cautioned that a policy-driven bounce is not the same as a recovery in the economy itself.[^1] My read: many Chinese families hold savings in shares, so falling markets hurt confidence and spending, which is why Beijing cares.

In technology, Bloomberg reports that Huawei will present a paper in February describing high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the fast memory stacked beside AI chips, with twice the data connections per area of chips mass-produced by Samsung and SK Hynix.[^3][^4] US rules bar Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron from selling HBM to Chinese buyers, so a home-grown version would ease a key bottleneck for China's AI chips. Conference papers often describe designs rather than finished products, and Huawei did not comment.[^3][^4]
